messages.author: b28a3b94cb6f8a9f
messages.subject: geom_point outline width
parts:
Hi,

I do not manage to control points outline width, neither using width
nor lwd…
qplot(1:3, 1:3, shape=1:3) and qplot(1:3, 1:3, shape=1:3, width=5)
give the same, while plot(1:3, 1:3, pch=1:3) and plot(1:3, 1:3,
pch=1:3, lwd=5) do not.

I really need to control this parameter as I am polishing plot at real
size (approx 10cm wide) and I cannot distinguish filled and open
circle.
Thank you in advance for your help,

Thomas

messages.subject: Re: geom_point outline width
parts:
Hi,

I don't think you can do it currently. You could try this modified
version of GeomPoint and see if it helps,

library(ggplot2)

GeomPoint$draw <- function (., data, scales, coordinates, na.rm = FALSE, ...)
{
data <- remove_missing(data, na.rm, c("x", "y", "size","width", "shape"),
name = "geom_point")
if (empty(data))
return(zeroGrob())
with(coordinates$transform(data, scales), ggname(.$my_name(),
pointsGrob(x, y, size = unit(size, "mm"), pch = shape,
gp = gpar(col = alpha(colour, alpha), fill = fill,
fontsize = size * ggplot2:::.pt, lex=width))))
}


GeomPoint$default_aes <- function (.)
aes(shape = 16, colour = "black", size = 2, fill = NA, alpha = 1,
width=1)

qplot(1:3, 1:3, shape=1:3, size=I(10))

qplot(1:3, 1:3, shape=1:3, width=I(2), size=I(10))


HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: geom_point outline width
parts:
On Fri, Feb 25, 2011 at 9:03 PM, tjulou <thomas...@gmail.com> wrote:
> This is it! Great…
> Thousands thanks  :)
>
>
> Any idea how I could display it also in the legend?

If it's only a fixed value, you could simply add the parameter to
GeomPoint$draw_legend,


GeomPoint$draw_legend <- function (., data, ...)
{
if (!is.null(data$fill) && !all(is.na(data$fill)) && data$shape ==
16) {
data$shape <- 21
}
data <- aesdefaults(data, .$default_aes(), list(...))
with(data, pointsGrob(0.5, 0.5, size = unit(size, "mm"),
pch = shape, gp = gpar(col = alpha(colour, alpha), fill = alpha(fill,
alpha), fontsize = size * .pt, lex=size)))
}


However, if you want to map a value to the line width you'll need to
define a new scale,

d <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=rnorm(10),f=rep(letters[1:2], each=5))

qplot(x,y, data=d, shape=f, width=x, size=I(10)) +
scale_shape_manual(value=c(1,2))


HTH,

baptiste
